impact: Some `.reviewbridge.json` config fields are accepted by the schema but not actually consumed downstream — silently no-op rather than rejected at load time. Surfaced during a pre-1.0.0 implementation review as a deferred medium issue. Specific fields not yet enumerated; an audit pass should grep config field references against actual usages and either wire them up or reject them in the loader. Not blocking 1.0.0 because no current user has reported a behavioral surprise; flagged so the audit can land in 1.0.x as a separate ticket.
resolution: Resolved by T-031 (commit b434a4f). Audited every review_standards field against its consumers. (1) Removed review_standards.code_review.max_file_size — it had zero consumers anywhere; chunking (max_chunk_tokens) superseded it. Non-strict parsing means existing configs with the key still load. (2) Wired review_standards.precommit.auto_diff — the precommit tool now falls back to it (args.auto_diff ?? config.review_standards.precommit.auto_diff) and the CLI gained --auto-diff/--no-auto-diff (precedence explicit --diff > flag > config); effective default unchanged. (3) The loader now WARNS (stderr, never rejects, no .strict()) on unrecognized keys at every level via a guarded plain-object descent, so a stale field surfaces instead of being an invisible no-op. The full field->consumer audit table is in the commit message. All other fields confirmed consumed. 8 new tests; full gate green. (Housekeeping: the ticket commit said 'Resolves ISS-004' but the issue status was not flipped at the time — closing it now.)
title: Config no-op fields: schema accepts settings that nothing reads
